Use linear coordinates whose last coordinate is the given nonzero height. Removing t times the transverse endpoint slope is a determinant-one linear shear in those coordinates. It fixes heights, commutes with Minkowski addition, and makes every point of S have one transverse coordinate x_0. Any common volume factor for the initial linear coordinates cancels in the inequality.

For full-dimensional polytope B, its transverse projection has dimension d-1≥1 and at least two distinct vertices. Outside the finite union of tied-value hyperplanes, exactly one vertex has the largest functional value, so the strict regions partition up to null sets and do not contain the zero vector. Each chosen vertex lift lies in B and has height at least -c.

For v in the region of p_i, evaluating the support functional at v+p_i gives |v|²+h_P(v)>h_P(v), putting the translate outside P. If two regions translated by p_i and p_j met, their strict maximizing inequalities would force (v-w) dot (p_i-p_j)>0, while the shared image would force it equal to -|p_i-p_j|². Thus the translated regions are disjoint.

Partition the upper tail by x-x_0. The discarded set lies over finitely many transverse hyperplanes, hence is null by Fubini. Each actual translation by a point of B sends its tail piece to height at least zero in A+B, outside the transverse projection of S+B. The translated pieces have disjoint transverse projections, so their volumes add, and S+B is contained in A+B.

Full-dimensional inscribed polytopes from a dense sequence approximate B in Hausdorff distance while preserving the height lower bound. With the fixed inscribed ball, lambda=epsilon/(rho+epsilon) makes (1-lambda)epsilon-lambda rho zero. The two support inequalities then give the claimed homothet inclusion. Adding the two homothets in the respective summands gives the nested Minkowski sums for D=A and D=S.

The nested sum volumes differ by at most [1-(1-lambda)^d] times the limiting volume for each D. That bound controls the error in each fixed halfspace capture and tends to zero, so the coefficient-one comparison survives the limit for the same upper tail.

In the box example both captured vertical lengths are h-c+epsilon because ell-c<0<h-c+epsilon. The difference of the transverse box volumes times this length gives the claimed formula. Its ratio to 2^(d-1)(h-c) tends to one. An exact d=3 check at ell=-2,h=3,c=1,epsilon=1/8 gives ratio 85/64. In dimension one the stated example has identical sums and positive tail length two. Even with proper containment S=[-2,5/2], the captured difference is only 1/2.

overlap.comparison: Its proof establishes the coefficient-one planar gain over a swept extreme-height segment in a canonical mixed-body configuration, by left and right endpoint gains. The current result works for arbitrary d≥2, any segment in A with distinct endpoint heights, and the sole lower constraint min_B t≥-c.

Uses Brunn–Minkowski for multiple disjoint residual sectors under canonical simplex inequalities. Its reserve is for whole mixed-body sectors and is not a difference between A+B and S+B at one height.

readability: The transverse normal regions encode translations by actual lifts of projection vertices. Their disjointness and separation from the projection of S+B supply both parts needed to count the entire tail once.
